title: The invention of the zipper: Judson's 1893 clasp locker, Sundback's 1913 redesign, and the 1923 galoshes that gave it its name

facts.text: Whitcomb Judson of Chicago came up with his slide fastener in 1893 because he was tired of lacing up his boots.
In 1893 Judson received U.S. patents for a fastener for shoes that was opened and closed by a slide; he called it a clasp locker.
Judson showed the clasp locker at the 1893 World's Fair in Chicago, but the public mostly paid no attention to it.
The early fastener was clumsy and often got stuck, although it did work.
Sales of the early fasteners were poor because they could pop open under strain and were sharp enough to tear cloth.
In 1894 Judson and a business partner, Lewis Walker, started a company to sell the fastener.
Gideon Sundback, an engineer born in Sweden, joined the fastener company in 1906.
In 1913 Sundback reworked Judson's fastener into a simpler and more reliable form; the most important change was getting rid of the hooks.
In 1917 Sundback received a patent for a metal fastener that already had the main features of the modern metal zipper.
In 1917 a tailor in New York made money belts with the new fastener; they were the first product made with it in large numbers and were popular with sailors during World War I.
During World War I, the U.S. Army also used the fasteners on soldiers' clothing and equipment.
Soon after World War I, the fastener began to appear on gloves and on pouches for carrying tobacco.
In 1923 the B.F. Goodrich company began selling rubber overshoes (galoshes) with the fastener, and this was probably the biggest push toward its popularity.
B.F. Goodrich made up the name zipper, based on the sound the fastener makes, and registered it as a trademark for its rubber footwear.
By the late 1920s, zippers were used on all kinds of clothing, shoes, and bags, and by the mid-1930s fashion designers had taken them up too.
Judson died in 1909, so he never heard the word zipper or saw his invention succeed.
Lewis Walker spent about 20 years and roughly one million dollars on the fastener before it finally sold well.
The gap between Judson's 1893 showing of the clasp locker and the 1923 zipper galoshes was 30 years.

notes: Sundback 1913 年的改良：Lemelson-MIT 寫 1913 年改造成更流線、更可靠的形式；Scientific American 寫 1917 年取得具備現代金屬拉鍊特徵的專利，並引述他說最需要的是去掉鉤子。選文只寫 1913 年改良、去掉鉤子，不寫專利細節（齒的數目等白名單來源沒有）。zipper 名稱是 B.F. Goodrich 依聲音取的（Lemelson-MIT：onomatopoeia）；近期學測已有「因聲音而得名」的正解，出題時不考名稱由來。
